question: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court of India impose a three-month deadline for the President to give assent to State Bills reserved under Article 201?

options.text: Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980)
SR Bommai vs. Union of India (1994)
State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)
Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973)

solution:
The correct answer is __**State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, in the landmark case of **State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)**, imposed a **three-month deadline** for the President to decide on State Bills reserved for consideration under **Article 201**.
 
• **Article 201** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the procedure for assent to bills reserved by the **Governor** for the consideration of the President. The President may either give assent or withhold assent to the bill.
 
• This judgment emphasizes the importance of preventing undue delays in the assent process for bills passed by state legislatures and reserved for the President's consideration. *Hence, this is the correct case.*
 
• This decision is significant in maintaining the federal structure of India, ensuring that the states' legislative processes are not hindered by indefinite delays in decision-making.
 
• The Supreme Court's ruling provides clarity on the procedure and timelines for decisions related to state bills, promoting accountability and efficiency in governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 201 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 201** empowers the President to either give assent to a bill reserved by the Governor or withhold assent.
 
• The article is designed to ensure that bills passed by state legislatures align with the central laws and policies. However, it does not specify any time frame for the President's decision, leading to delays in some cases.
 
• The Supreme Court's ruling in **2023** sets a precedent by introducing a **three-month deadline** for the President to decide, ensuring better legislative efficiency.
 
 
 
• **State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023):**
 
 
• This case highlights the issue of delays in decision-making regarding bills reserved under **Article 201.**
 
• The judgment reinforces the principle of cooperative federalism, ensuring that state legislations are not indefinitely stalled.
 
• It serves as a benchmark for similar cases in the future, bringing clarity to the process of granting assent to state bills.
 
 
 
• **Other Landmark Cases:**
 
 
• **Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980):** This case dealt with the balance between fundamental rights and directive principles but did not address Article 201.
 
• **SR Bommai vs. Union of India (1994):** This case focused on the application of President's Rule and federalism, not Article 201.
 
• **Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973):** This case was pivotal in establishing the Basic Structure Doctrine but did not involve Article 201.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Significance:**

 
 
• The judgment in **State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)** underscores the importance of timely decision-making in the legislative process.
 
• By imposing a **three-month deadline**, the Supreme Court ensures that governance at the state level is not compromised due to procedural delays.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Federalism:**
 
 
• The case strengthens the concept of **cooperative federalism**, where both the Center and States work in harmony without undue interference.
 
• It provides a clear framework for handling bills under **Article 201**, fostering trust and transparency between the state and central authorities.
